name: Isovist Properties as Visual Prediction Range and Spatial Monitoring Capacity
panel_source: SPATIAL-I (Sprint 13.17) — upgrades SC-I structural YAML (Doc 38) and SC-II partial calibration (Doc 62)

mechanism_chain.description: Isovist area at any point is defined geometrically by the spatial configuration (walls, columns, screens) and the occupant's position and orientation. Isovist area is the total visible floor area from that point.

data.finding: Isovist field is defined geometrically by wall positions, column positions, and observer location

justification.backing: Step 1 is definitional — the isovist is a geometric property of the building at each point. No mechanism claim is being made.
justification.qualifier: Definitional step — confidence inherent to the geometric framework.

mechanism_chain.description: Large isovist area → visual cortex receives rich, spatially extended input → primary visual cortex (V1) encodes the full visible scene; scene-processing areas (PPA: parahippocampal place area) construct a confident scene model → the spatial prediction system has extensive sensory evidence and generates confident predictions about space beyond the visible boundary.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: V1, V2, V3 hierarchical visual processing; LOC (lateral occipital complex) object recognition at isovist boundary; PPA (parahippocampal place area) scene-level encoding (Epstein & Kanwisher, 1998)

data.finding: PPA constructs scene models from visual input; scene encoding is automatic and robust
data.effect: PPA responds selectively to scenes and spatial layouts

data.finding: Isovist area correlates with occupant preference for openness/comfort at r ≈ 0.48

justification.backing: Penn's two-claim structure: Claim A (isovist-preference: EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE at 0.60, panel accepted) and Claim B (visual prediction mechanism: MECHANISM at 0.45, mechanism well-grounded but not directly measured in architectural space). Shahar pushed A down from 0.65 to 0.60 because Stamps meta covers enclosure preference generally, not architecturally-instrumented isovist measurements specifically.
justification.qualifier: Confidence split: 0.60 for the behavioral correlation (established), 0.45 for the specific prediction mechanism (grounded in visual neuroscience but not directly tested with architectural isovist manipulation in fMRI/EEG). Penn accepted both values.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) isovist area preference reflects simple spaciousness preference (more room = more comfortable) without any prediction computation — pure space preference without PE; (b) the correlation is dominated by window views (large isovists often include windows → nature views → L-template and VIEW1 effects confound the isovist-specific contribution).

mechanism_chain.description: Each occluding edge at the isovist boundary generates a PREDICTIVE COMPLETION demand: the visual system must predict what lies behind each edge (Rao & Ballard, 1999; Lee & Nguyen, 2001). Prediction accuracy depends on global spatial knowledge (from the cognitive map — SC1) and local geometric inference (from the edge geometry and prior scene context). More occluding edges = more concurrent predictions = higher prediction demand.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: V2, V4 feedback pathways for predictive boundary completion; hippocampal recall of previously-viewed spaces to inform predictions about occluded regions; ACC (anterior cingulate) monitoring prediction-perception mismatch

data.finding: V2,V4 feedback pathways support predictive boundary completion at occluding edges
data.effect: V2/V4 boundary completion signals for occluded regions

data.finding: More occluding edges = more concurrent predictions = higher prediction demand
data.effect: Prediction load proportional to occluding edge count

justification.backing: The visual system DOES fill in occluded regions with predictions (Rao & Ballard, Lee & Nguyen). Penn's architectural application: "the isovist IS the visual prediction range, and occluding edges ARE the boundaries where prediction must substitute for perception." This is well-grounded in visual neuroscience but not directly confirmed in architectural isovist-varying conditions.
justification.qualifier: MECHANISM warrant at confidence 0.45 (Penn accepted). The mechanism is well-grounded but the specific architectural application — that occluding edge count in buildings drives measurable prediction demand — has not been directly tested.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) architectural occluding edges are too complex (textured, irregular) for the clean boundary completion mechanisms studied in visual neuroscience labs; (b) occupants in familiar buildings have already learned what lies behind each edge, rendering the prediction load negligible after initial exposure.

mechanism_chain.description: Small isovists with many occluding edges trigger THREAT MONITORING via T5 pathway: limited visual access means threats cannot be detected at distance. The amygdala responds to spatial constriction and limited exit visibility with elevated threat assessment. This produces physiological arousal (GSR elevation, cortisol increase under prolonged exposure) independent of any actual threat.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Amygdala (basolateral nucleus) threat assessment from limited visual field; HPA axis activation under sustained spatial constriction (T5 mechanism); superior colliculus orienting reflex toward isovist edges (potential threat locations)

data.finding: Amygdala responds to spatial constriction and limited exit visibility with threat assessment
data.source: Inferred from threat monitoring literature: LeDoux (1996); Whalen (1998)
data.effect: Amygdala activation for limited visual access conditions

data.finding: Prospect-Refuge theory: large forward isovist (prospect) preferred; concealment behind (refuge)
data.effect: Preference for prospect-refuge configuration across cultures

justification.backing: The threat monitoring step integrates Prospect-Refuge (evolutionary grounding for the isovist preference) with amygdala threat detection neuroscience. Penn: "Prospect-Refuge gives the evolutionary motivation... that theoretical grounding raises the OVERALL confidence in the framework." Shahar agreed: "The evolutionary background raises the plausibility of the causal claim without changing the confidence in the specific parameter estimate."
justification.qualifier: FUNCTIONAL warrant for prospect-refuge at bridge_prior 0.50. The evolutionary argument is plausible but the specific parameter values (optimal prospect ≥30m², refuge <5m² posterior) are THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — derived from Appleton conceptual framework with sparse direct measurement.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) the prospect-refuge preference is culturally constructed (savanna experience) rather than evolved — urban populations might show different isovist preferences; (b) amygdala threat assessment requires actual threat cues, not merely limited visual access — small isovists in familiar, safe environments might not trigger threat monitoring.

mechanism_chain.description: Isovist drift (change in isovist configuration as the occupant moves) generates continuous spatial PE: new regions enter the prediction range as the isovist advances; regions previously predicted must be verified. Smooth drift (curves, gradual reveals) produces continuous low-magnitude PE; sharp drift (corners, doorways) produces discontinuous high-magnitude PE at the moment of isovist snap.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Posterior parietal cortex (PPC) spatial updating during movement; hippocampal theta oscillations synchronizing with movement rhythm (Jacobs et al., 2010); LC noradrenergic spike at isovist discontinuity — novelty signal

data.finding: Hippocampal theta oscillations synchronize with movement rhythm during spatial navigation
data.effect: Theta frequency locked to movement pace

data.finding: Sharp isovist transitions (corners, doorways) produce LC noradrenergic novelty spikes
data.source: Theoretical integration from predictive coding + LC physiology
data.paradigm: Predictive processing framework applied to spatial transitions

justification.backing: Isovist drift (smooth change during movement) produces continuous low-PE spatial updating. Isovist snap (abrupt change at threshold) produces discontinuous high-PE — the basis for SC3's compression-release mechanism. The distinction between drift and snap is the boundary between comfortable spatial experience and arousing architectural events.
justification.qualifier: MECHANISM warrant. The drift/snap distinction is well-motivated by the difference between smooth predictive updating and abrupt prediction violation. Confidence limited by the lack of direct measurement of LC-NE burst during architectural isovist transitions.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) occupants in buildings do not experience isovist transitions as "events" because their attention is on tasks, conversations, or phones rather than spatial processing — the PE signal may be below attentional threshold in normal building use.

spatial_configuration.construct: GSR peak at abrupt isovist transition (corner-turning, doorway crossing) as function of isovist area ratio

coefficient.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — empirically anchored by Kuliga VR (N=48) and Ellard ambulatory data but scaling coefficient has wide CI (±0.15)

spatial_configuration.functional_form_warrant: MECHANISM — logarithmic Weber-Fechner psychophysics of proportional stimulus change (Fechner, 1860); established across sensory modalities; architectural application is a theoretically-grounded extension

anxiety_disorder_history.modifier: +0.15 to +0.25 μS elevation across all ratios — heightened threat-detection sensitivity

architect_professional.modifier: -0.10 to -0.15 μS — professional spatial literacy reduces the surprise magnitude of transitions; cognitive map formed from floor plan study before visit

nature_view_quality.construct: Isovist configuration producing maximum occupant preference: large forward isovist (prospect) combined with partial concealment of self (refuge element)

optimal_prospect_isovist_area.unit: m² visible floor area in forward hemisphere
optimal_prospect_isovist_area.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — derived from Appleton (1975) conceptual framework; direct measurement sparse

optimal_refuge_condition.description: Solid wall or substantial barrier behind occupant with isovist area <5m² in posterior hemisphere

nature_view_quality.note: The prospect-refuge balance is a design principle with evolutionary grounding but poorly parameterized empirically for contemporary buildings. Article Eater should treat this parameter as a qualitative evaluative criterion rather than a precise quantitative input until calibration studies are completed.

ie_dpt_interaction.mechanism: The implicit channel continuously evaluates isovist properties for threat indicators — small area, many occluding edges, limited exit visibility — and generates implicit safety ratings. This is the perceptual instantiation of Prospect-Refuge as an implicit heuristic rather than an explicit calculation. The explicit channel (T_IE_003) engages when implicit monitoring flags an isovist configuration below the safety threshold.

primary: Healthcare (patient-room visual access; corridor isovist design)
Museums and galleries (isovist sequence as curatorial tool)
secondary: Residential (bedroom and living space isovist comfort)
low_applicability: Industrial (occupancy patterns non-sedentary, threat monitoring non-primary)
Parking structures (isovist below comfort threshold by design necessity)

### Template VIEW1: Nature View as Multi-Channel Prediction Confirmation

name: "Nature View as Multi-Channel Prediction Confirmation — How Visual Access to Natural Environments Produces Convergent Stress Reduction, Attention Restoration, and Positive Affect"

structural_pattern: >
  A window view of nature engages multiple PE mechanisms
  simultaneously, producing a convergent effect that exceeds
  the sum of individual channels. This structural parallel to
  L3 (daylight convergence) and MAT4 (wood convergence) is the
  template's central insight: nature views are powerful not
  because of any single mechanism but because they confirm
  predictions across MANY channels at once.
  
  FIVE CONVERGENT CHANNELS:
  
  CHANNEL 1 — FRACTAL FLUENCY (T1): Natural scenes exhibit
  1/f spatial frequency profiles with fractal dimension near
  D ≈ 1.3 (Taylor et al., 2011). This matches the visual
  system's processing structure, producing maximal processing
  fluency and minimal visual PE. Trees, clouds, water surfaces,
  and terrain all exhibit fractal statistics. Built environments
  typically exhibit non-fractal statistics (regular geometry,
  flat surfaces, periodic repetition). The nature view confirms
  the visual system's deep prediction for natural spatial
  statistics.
  
  CHANNEL 2 — PROSPECT AND SPATIAL DEPTH (SC2/T5): Nature
  views typically provide spatial depth (long isovist) with
  vegetative partial enclosure — the prospect-refuge combination
  that Appleton (1975) identified and SC2 formalizes. The
  ability to see far (prospect) with the protection of an
  enclosed space (refuge through the building itself) confirms
  the spatial prediction for safety: the occupant can monitor
  the environment for threats and opportunities while being
  protected. A view of a brick wall provides neither prospect
  nor spatial depth.
  
  CHANNEL 3 — ATTENTION RESTORATION (T25/ART): Natural scenes
  engage "soft fascination" — involuntary attention to gently
  interesting stimuli (moving leaves, drifting clouds, flowing
  water) that permits directed attention to rest and recover
  (Kaplan, 1995). This is the attentional Goldilocks zone:
  enough engagement to prevent disengagement, insufficient
  demand to deplete directed attention. A blank wall provides
  no fascination; a busy urban scene provides hard fascination
  that demands effortful processing.
  
  CHANNEL 4 — TEMPORAL VARIATION (L5): Nature views are
  inherently dynamic: wind moves branches, clouds shift,
  light changes, seasons transform the scene. This dynamic
  variation provides the temporal PE that L5 formalizes —
  gradual, natural change that maintains interest without
  producing surprise. The view of nature is a built-in
  dynamic light and pattern display that changes continuously
  through the day and across seasons.
  
  CHANNEL 5 — ECOLOGICAL SAFETY SIGNAL: Green vegetation,
  water, and spatial openness are evolutionary signals of
  a resource-rich, safe environment (Ulrich et al., 1991).
  This is the biophilia/SRT mechanism: the presence of
  nature signals environmental safety, reducing HPA axis
  activation (T5) and contributing to allostatic balance
  (T29). Built environments lack this signal; degraded
  environments (dead vegetation, polluted water) may
  invert it.
  
  CONVERGENCE: Each channel contributes a modest individual
  effect. The convergent total — all five channels confirming
  predictions simultaneously — produces a strong, multi-
  mechanism benefit that explains why nature views consistently
  produce measurable health outcomes (Ulrich, 1984; White
  et al., 2019) while individual mechanisms produce smaller
  effects in isolation. The structural parallel to L3 and
  MAT4 is deliberate: MULTI-CHANNEL CONVERGENCE IS A GENERAL
  PRINCIPLE of how natural stimuli produce strong effects.

IC2_body_budget.interaction: Small isovists (high occluding-edge density) chronically activate the threat monitoring pathway (T5) and generate interoceptive arousal signals registered by IC2 as elevated body budget demand. Prolonged occupancy in small-isovist spaces — enclosed cubicles, narrow corridors, basement offices — produces measurable allostatic cost via sustained low-grade threat arousal.
IC2_body_budget.direction: SC2 feeds IC2 as upstream trigger; effect cumulative with SC4 social monitoring load

AX4_perceived_control.interaction: Isovist area directly determines occupant's perceived spatial control: large isovist → can see multiple exits, monitor the full space → high AX4 (spatial agency). Small isovist → exits may be concealed, space beyond is opaque → reduced AX4. This is the spatial basis of AX4 in building interiors — the most architecturally tractable lever for AX4 modification.
AX4_perceived_control.direction: SC2 feeds AX4 as primary architectural determinant of spatial visual agency
